messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] issue with MKL
messages.body_plain:
Your question is not clear.

You ask: what next? the answer is usually that you submit a new revision of the package, so no matter how small the fixes you need to increment the package version number (typically a patchlevel update) to get a response from CRAN.

You ask what to do with an issue? It is extremely difficult for some random person on this list (much less the rare person who might have an answer to your problem) to answer that... you are setting yourself up to be ignored by not providing a CRAN link to the most recent build output that had your implemented fixes. If you don't have this then see the previous paragraph.

This is a generic response by a random non-expert in MKL problems in the hope that with a proper query you can catch the attention of an actual expert. Best of luck...

messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] issue with MKL
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for all the feedback. The issues were resolved as CRAN accepted the
updated version (11.11.28) of my package yesterday. An error was
triggered when I interrupted the testthat procedures on my package. I do
routine checks especially when there are updates from some of the
dependencies. The testing normally lasted for about 17 minutes so once the
lines are evaluated and passed, I stop the procedure. So a CRAN member
caught the interruption as an error because two lines of code given
different values of the same function, for example, XXXXXXXXXXXX32 not
equivalent to XXXXXXXXXXXX36. And the error was said to be caused by a new
version of MKL. I immediately allowed the full procedure and nothing was
wrong but I demobilised the two lines. And CRAN was adamant, insisting on
me addressing the error. I then dug into MKL and updated the version and
still could not pacify CRAN, the reason for the cry out.

Job N Nmadu. *Jesus cares*!
